title: 5.4.5 Lab: Pipes that come and go
description: The starter builds one pair of pipes and leaves it. Build a new pair on a timer, keep them in an array, and delete the ones that have left the screen.

steps.title: Build a pair on a timer
steps.instructions: The function `makePipe()` is given: it builds one pair and returns the top pipe. In `draw()`, call it every 90 frames and put the result in the `pipes` array. Run it: pipes should keep arriving from the right.

steps.title: Delete the pipes that have gone
steps.instructions: Loop over `pipes` from the end to the start. When a pipe's `x` is less than -30, delete its `mate` and the pipe itself, and splice it out of the array.
hints: `for (let i = pipes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { ... }` is the backwards loop from 5.4.4.

steps.title: Show how many are alive
steps.instructions: Draw `pipes.length` on the screen. It should rise to two or three and then hold there. If it keeps climbing, pipes are not being removed.

requirements.title: A pair is built on a repeating beat
requirements.description: A remainder test on the frame count builds a pair at a steady rate. Help: 5.4.4 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

requirements.title: Every pair goes into the array
requirements.description: The new pipe is pushed so the game can find it again. Help: 5.4.4 (Reading: A world that scrolls)

requirements.title: Pipes that have left are deleted and spliced out
requirements.description: The sprite is deleted and also taken out of the array. Help: 5.4.4 (Reading: A world that scrolls)
